solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Way, however harsh, to progress

parts.note: tho is an informal short spelling of though, meaning however
to fare is to get on or progress, as in 'how did you fare?'

explanation.surface: A moralising line: whatever the hardship, one must keep moving forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A main road or public street is a way through a place, a synonym.

clue.text: Send for publication … and then tuck in?

definitions.meaning: in printing, a newspaper edition is finalised and sent to press
a child is tucked into bed at night by a parent

explanation.surface: An editor finishes the paper and then settles the children down for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is newspaper jargon for completing an edition, and literally means settling someone into bed.

clue.text: Use a spoon for porridge

definitions.meaning: to mix something round with a spoon
British slang for a prison sentence, doing time

explanation.surface: Breakfast instructions: take a spoon to the oats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porridge' is British slang for time in prison, as is the answer; both are also kitchen words, which hides the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Mixing with a spoon is the verb sense; prison is the slang noun sense shared with porridge.

clue.text: Eyes a commission coming up involving Irish playwright

indicators.note: coming up says the hidden letters are read backwards
involving means the words take in, and so contain, the letters wanted

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone eyes a commission that is about to involve an Irish dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'involving', but that word is the hidden-word signal; the definition is just 'Irish playwright'. In a down clue 'coming up' reads the letters from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Sean O'Casey was the Dublin dramatist of Juno and the Paycock, an example of the category.

clue.text: Irritable, not having finished note

indicators.note: not finished means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A cranky person leaves a note half-written.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarter note in music is called by this British name, an example of a note.

clue.text: Area that's sacred, inside boundaries

indicators.note: inside the boundaries means take the letters within the word's first and last

explanation.surface: A patch of holy ground marked off by its borders.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of land measure, so a quantity of surface area.

clue.text: Often visit area in course of search

indicators.note: in the course of means placed in the middle of the other word

explanation.surface: Someone keeps returning to a district while looking for something.
explanation.definitionFit: To frequent a place, as a ghost or a regular does, is this verb.

clue.text: Hard skin on foot, chest or back, initially, or part of ear

parts.note: a corn is a patch of thickened skin on a toe

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A medical checklist moving from foot to chest to back to ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ear' looks anatomical, like the rest, but it is an ear of maize.
explanation.definitionFit: The woody core on which the kernels of a maize ear grow is a component of it.

clue.text: Part of underground movement in a rebellion ok

indicators.note: movement means the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: An underground resistance movement approves of a rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bakerloo line is one of the London Underground lines; 'underground' suggests secret resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the routes of the London Tube network, an example.

clue.text: Profits from this unsold merchandise?

definitions.meaning: yields or gains on an investment
goods sent back to the supplier or publisher because they did not sell

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper wonders whether any gain can come from stock nobody bought.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means investment yields, and also unsold copies sent back, as with newspapers.

clue.text: Little change in patient, ultimately feeble

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A doctor notes only a slight shift in a patient who is still frail.
explanation.definitionFit: A small adjustment or fine-tuning is a minor change.

clue.text: Man hurt by shot? Don't believe it

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or broken, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A report of a man wounded by a gunshot, dismissed as untrue.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a dismissive phrase: the answer is a story people repeat but should not believe.
explanation.definitionFit: A widely told but false modern tale is something not to be credited.

clue.text: Unrelated to comedian Bob? Some chance!

definitions.meaning: Bob Hope was the American comedian; someone not of his family is literally not one of that name
an ironic exclamation meaning there is no chance at all

explanation.surface: Asked whether they are kin to Bob Hope, someone scoffs.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for no chance whatever, and literally says not a member of the Hope family.

clue.text: Express article one runs

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A newspaper item about a single athlete who runs, in the Express.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' looks like the newspaper title but is a verb, to voice.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice an opinion publicly is to give it an airing.

clue.text: Skill of boy if meeting wintry conditions

parts.note: Art is a short form of the boy's name Arthur
ice is a feature of wintry weather

explanation.surface: Asks what a boy could do if caught in frost and snow.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleverness or craft in contriving something, a synonym for skill.

clue.text: Returned note that's for builder to carry?

indicators.note: returned means the word is read backwards

parts.note: doh is the first note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A builder sends back a message about what to carry.
explanation.definitionFit: A bricklayer's open trough on a pole holds bricks or mortar carried on the shoulder.

clue.text: Line on rugby pitch that all the soccer players make

definitions.meaning: the line marked that many metres from each try line in rugby
two football teams of eleven together number this many

explanation.surface: Comparing markings on a rugby field with the players on a football field.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugby field has a line of this name, and both soccer elevens add up to this number.

clue.text: Repeated chapter appearing in English dictionary

indicators.note: appearing in means placed inside the other letters

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

explanation.surface: A chapter turns up twice in an English dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound bouncing back is repeated, so said again is a synonym.

clue.text: A long letter

parts.note: to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: A lengthy piece of correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective describing the letter, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the spelt-out name of the eighth letter of the alphabet, H.

clue.text: Instant credit

definitions.meaning: a moment, as in 'just a second'
buying on account, informal British usage, as in 'on the slate'

explanation.surface: An advertisement for credit available straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a moment of time, and in British slang buying on account.

clue.text: Problem that's as much as you can grasp?

definitions.meaning: a person or thing that is hard to manage

definitions.text: as much as you can grasp?
definitions.meaning: the quantity a hand can hold

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a difficulty that is just within one's reach.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricky child is called this, and it also means the amount one hand holds.

clue.text: Arrests outlaw turning up with son

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it

explanation.surface: A fugitive appears with his son and police make arrests.
explanation.definitionFit: To nab is informal for catch or seize, so a verb for arrests.

clue.text: One who's got out of PE: cease to be shocked!

indicators.note: shocked means jolted out of place, so the letters move about

explanation.surface: A pupil has escaped gym class and is told to stop being outraged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got out of PE' tempts as the definition, but PE is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has broken free from captivity is a person who has got out.

clue.text: Scholarly monk saved or successfully brought home?

definitions.meaning: Roger ..., the thirteenth-century Franciscan friar and philosopher
the idioms 'save one's ...' and 'bring home the ...'

explanation.surface: A learned friar who either rescued something or carried it back triumphantly.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition points to two British idioms: to save your bacon (escape harm) and to bring home the bacon (succeed, or earn a living).
explanation.definitionFit: Roger Bacon was a learned medieval friar; the cured meat is what is saved or brought home in two idioms.
